author: atarasov <lomereiter@gmail.com>
commit message:
Better read correction evaluation.

Raw and corrected reads are mapped to the same reference with tmap,
then compared.

hammer-it now prints to stderr all clusters that have 2 or more
kmers with count >50.

clusters.rb converts them into FASTA format, maintaining cluster
indices. These k-mers are then mapped to the specified region
of the reference.

cluster_summaries takes as input BAM file with mapped k-mers
(sorted by read name) and prints information about most frequent
k-mers in each cluster (sequence, position on the reference, CIGAR,
NM and MD tags)

comparator outputs not only the report, but also BAM files with
erroneously corrected reads, which can be examined later.

commit message:
Correction algorithm based on merging chunks with good consensus.

New algorithm tries to preserve read length (% corrected errors).
Chunks are composed of subsequent 'good' hkmer cluster centers,
and aligned later against the read. If they don't overlap,
the part of the read between their respective ends is copied as is;
the case of overlap is not yet finished (scores are to be taken
into account) - this is one of main error sources, the other one
is absence of subclustering.

Do not use the same counter for warnings and errors.

however errors, if enabled, should not be ignored. Currently since warnings
and errors share the same counter we effectively stop showing errors after
16 warnings (which happen all the time).

Use different counters for errors and warnings.

commit message:
start relative poses at their final target frame

For relative poses, transform the initial input pose by targetFrameTrans before storing it, thus making relative poses start at 0 with regard to the final target frame, rather than their own reference frame.

An example application is an IMU that is mounted the wrong way up. Previously, the resulting initial (relative) pose would have put the robot upside-down!

author: Ivor Wanders <ivor@iwanders.net>
commit message:
Add reporting of bad timestamps via diagnostics

The first situation which is reported is if the timestamp is before or equal to
 the timestamp of the last pose reset. This report is also triggered when the
 timestamp is empty (zero) since `lastSetPoseTime_` is also initialised to zero.

The second situation which is reported is when a message is received that has
 a timestamp prior to the last message received for that topic.

In both situations the behaviour of the filter is to disregard the message and
 reporting this via diagnostics should be useful.

This resolves #224.

author: Simon Gene Gottlieb <s.gottlieb@fu-berlin.de>
commit message:
preperation for nodelets

This diff applies changes to the structure on how the nodes work. The goal
is to have a structure that allows laterone to transform them into
nodelets.

To archive nodelet compatible structure, I have to remove *::run() methods and the
while(ros::ok()); loops.

The current run method has actually two parts:
  1. initialization
  2. the main loop

Because of this I decided to move the initialization part into a own
function. The main loop is put into a "periodicUpdate"
function, which is registerd with a ros timer for periodic call.

This is done for navsat_transformation_node and ukf/ekf_localiaztion_nodes.

adds nodelet for ukf and ekf

NodeHandle and private NodeHandle from RosFilter and NavSatTransform into
the main function and the Nodelet implementation.

ekf_localization can be used with easy switch between node and nodelet

in euler angle representation. This was an issue in IMUTwistBasicIO.

Instead of comparing Euler Angles, quaternion are being compared, making
the test much more reliable.

commit message:
Allow to use safe clampRotation (normalization)

The ROBOT_LOCALIZATION_USE_FAST_CLAMP_ROTATION allows to use the current
fast implementation that assumes the angles are close to normalized (ON)
or the slightly slower but safer (no assumptions)
angles::normalize_angle implementation (OFF); defaults to ON.

Note that if the angle is huge, the fast implementation will get into an
infinite loop because adding or removing TAU (2 * M_PI) for a huge
number won't change its value, because of the numerical precision, so
the filter will take 100% CPU and will never return from the infinite
loop.

author: Enrique Fernandez <efernandez@clearpath.ai>
commit message:
Don't clear globalCallbackQueue on set pose

fixes CORE-10163

Clearing the callback queue doesn't clear the subscriber queue, leading
to a full queue and no new messages issued into the user callbacks.
See https://github.com/ros/ros_comm/issues/1169

The underlying issue in ros_comm isn't trivial to solve, so it's better
not to clear. After all, all the callbacks already check if the
measurements time stamps are older than the last set pose timestamp, so
they're ignored.

commit message:
Enable build optimisations if no build type configured.

The selected build type can have a significant influence on processor usage (tenths of %). As setting a build type is often forgotten by users, from-source builds of robot_localization on resource constraint platforms can run into issues of low update rates, starvation and issues with stability.

If a build type is configured (on the ROS buildfarm fi), the added stanzas respect it and do not overwrite it. If nothing is configured, a warning is printed and the CMake-standard `RelWithDebInfo` type is configured.

commit message:
Fix warning "Failed to meet update rate!"

Commit EDC5BEA from April 2020 causes an access to the ros parameter
server for every IMU packet that is processed. If the ros parameter
server is not local, the fetch time can lead to lost input messages,
and erratic timing of filter updates.

The fix is to fetch the parameter silent_tf_failure only once at startup.
This addresses issue #601.

commit message:
Fix runtime exception thrown when parameter override not provided

The templated declare_parameter method needs an override (or default value) since
it returns the actual parameter value, otherwise we get an exception.
To correctly declare a parameter without a default value, we should use a different
signature.

Related upstream issue: https://github.com/ros2/rclcpp/issues/1691

Signed-off-by: Jacob Perron <jacob@openrobotics.org>

author: Chris Lalancette <clalancette@gmail.com>
commit message:
Switch robot_localization to modern CMake idioms.

Some of these have been best practice for a while, and
some of them will become best practice in the near future.

1. Move the include directory down one-level.  This is to better
support overlays and underlays; see https://github.com/ros2/ros2/issues/1150
for the entire saga.  The upshot is that all includes should be
one more directory level down, and CMake will handle the differences.
This has been best practice since Humble.

2. Switch from ament_target_dependencies() to target_link_libraries().
ament_target_dependencies was developed in the days before
target_link_libraries() was fully capable, and nowadays
target_link_libraries() is a superset of the functionality.  There is
one oddity here, in that in order to deal with ROS message packages, we
have to use ${<msg_pkg_name>_TARGETS}, rather than the traditional CMake
target like msg_pkg_name::msg_pkg_name.  This is a bug in ROS that will
eventually be fixed.

3. Export a CMake target from robot_localization.  This means that
downstream packages will be able to use
target_link_libraries(<target> robot_localization::robot_localization)

4. Export all dependencies with ament_export_dependencies.  This ensures
that downstream project which rely on this one will be able to find
all of the includes.

Signed-off-by: Chris Lalancette <clalancette@gmail.com>

commit message:
Do not collapse trivial connections in Paths

fixes #131.

i.e., do not reglue bits in a ContourComponent with collapsed edges. If
we do so we loose vertices in the contour. Also this leads to trouble in
the IET induction process: When a SaddleConnection is found later, it
might cross such a vertex, therefore triggering an assertion since
saddle connections are not allowed to cross a marked vertex (even if
its total angle is 2π.)

author: Julian Rüth <julian.rueth@fsfe.org>
commit message:
Remove smart pointers from API

having the separation between stack and heap objects is weird and seems
a bit random in the API. Basically, it exposes underlying implementation
details, e.g., a SaddleConnection needs to hold on to the surface it's
defined on and therefore holds a smart pointer to it. Consequently, all
surfaces are passed by shared_ptr. A downside of this is that we
essentially need to discourage people from calling the actual
constructors of these objects (or hide them away completely) since
everything needs to be created through make_shared. Futhermore, cppyy
has (understandably) trouble with our methods that return unique_ptr
which they merely do to emphasize that they return a fresh unrelated
copy of a surface.

So, let's hide these memory issue away in the PIMPL so that surfaces
feel like any other stack allocated object (even though they are now
always shared pointers behind the scenes.)

Also renamed some names that had been bothering for a while such as slot
which is now called slit (fixes #114) and fromEdge which is now called
fromHalfEdge.

author: Lutti Antoine <antoinelutti@chuv.ch>
commit message:
f hmri_def.qMRI_maps.QA is set to 1 in the default file (default), the
toolbox outputs a QualityAssessment matlab structure that provides
objective measures of data quality. Contains the following fields :
- ContrastCoreg: values of the coregistration parameters (translations and rotations) of the MTw and T1w to the PDw. Measure of inter-scan motion.
- SDR2s: contains estimates of the standard deviation of the R2s maps calculated for each contrast (MTw, T1w and PDw) in white matter. Measure of intra-scan motion (Castella R et al., OHBM 2016; Arn L et al., OHBM 2016; Castella R et al., in prep.)
- PD: mean and SD of the A map in white matter following bias-field correction. Primarily a measure of the efficacy of the bias-field correction i.e. of the level of bias in the PD map from the receive sensitivity profile.

If hmri_def.qMRI_maps.ACPCrealign is set to 1 in the default file (default), the toolbox modifies the header of the qMRI maps to realign the AC-PC line to MNI space using SPM’s ‘avg152T1’ canonical template. The coordinate transform is saved in a ACPCrealign.mat structure to allow the user to undo the transformation if necessary.

author: ebalteau <e.balteau@ulg.ac.be>
commit message:
Output directories

To conciliate the various comments, opinions, requests, here is the
current organisation:

- Calc folders as before (B1mapCalc, MPMCalc, RFsensCalc) to be deleted at
  the end of the processing if cleanup==true.
- Results folder now contains
    - in the root directory (Results): the four final maps that will be
      analysed in the processing part of the toolbox, i.e.:
         - PD map (or A map if no PD map calculated)
	 - MT map
	 - R1 map (the most unbiased one available, i.e. fully
	   B1-bias-corrected, or UNICORT, or semi-quantitative if no B1
	   correction whatsoever)
	 - R2s map (R2s_OLS one if available, simple R2s otherwise)

    - in the Results/Supplementary directory:
         - moved all other images, i.e. B1 maps, simple R2s if R2s_OLS
	   available, semi-quantitative R1 if UNICORT applied, PPDw and
	   PT1w average images.
	 - all processing parameters and other json output files.

This way, basic users are not confused by multiple versions of maps
otherwise present in the same Results directory, and more advanced users
can access useful information and maps in Results/Supplementary for troubleshooting of other
purposes.

Use new recommendations for US in UNICORT

The settings tissue(1).ngaus = tissue(2).ngaus = 2 were the defaults in
unified segmentation until February 2013. These were used for the UNICORT paper (published 2010).

New defaults (John Ashburner, Rev. 5248 on the SVN repository) are tissue(1).ngaus = tissue(2).ngaus = 1.

The warp.cleanup and warp.mrf parameters were not used in 2010. Setting
them to 0 or 1 doesn't change the UNICORT results (Tobias Leutritz). Now
set to the current defaults (warp.mrf = warp.cleanup = 1).

commit message:
Module for visual inspection of the results

Three types of visualisation are possible:
- automated intensity scaling for all images (to check e.g. reorientation
  comparing input image and template)
- identical intensity scaling for all images (to check e.g. series of
  echoes from a T1w acquisition)
- standard scaling as defined for each output map (R1, R2*, MT, PD, B1,
  RFsens). Scaling is automated (between percentiles 5 and 95) if image
  type cannot be determined. Allows for quick visual check of any obvious
  anomaly in the output maps.

author: Luke Edwards <lukejoele+github@gmail.com>
commit message:
MPM quality check tool from @EvelyneBalteau (#39)

* Module for visual inspection of the results

Three types of visualisation are possible:
- automated intensity scaling for all images (to check e.g. reorientation
  comparing input image and template)
- identical intensity scaling for all images (to check e.g. series of
  echoes from a T1w acquisition)
- standard scaling as defined for each output map (R1, R2*, MT, PD, B1,
  RFsens). Scaling is automated (between percentiles 5 and 95) if image
  type cannot be determined. Allows for quick visual check of any obvious
  anomaly in the output maps.

* Few adjustments

- range for RF sensitivity maps [0 2]
- backward/forward compatibility between very last version of SPM and previous ones
- to handle B1+ and RFsens maps imtype

* Bug fixes and backward compatibility

- Depending on the history of manipulating the st.centre field, the latter can either be a column or a line vector. Elements processed one by one to avoid problems.
- strsplit and strjoin were added to Matlab from version R2013a. Alternative implementation for that specific case.

commit message:
Improve aitoff and altaz2hadec

Bring back `aitoff' to original simple definition with only scalar
arguments, then vectorize it by writing an explicit simple wrapper
around it taking arrays as argument.  This is more efficient than
writing a single function for both scalar and array arguments.  Do the
same for `altaz2hadec'.

In addition, use `@vectorize_1arg' macro for `airtovac', the resulting
macro is more efficient than using `map'.

Thanks to Kyle Barbary for suggestions!

commit message:
Update RLW_arrange_channels.m

In this way, channels are selected based on the label and not on the index in the data matrix. This solves the problem that appears when a group of datasets have different number of channels (e.g. when a noisy channel was removed in some but not all datasets). In the previous version, the script would look in the indexes of the first dataset, which could match or not the indexes in the rest of the selected datasets.

author: michal <michal.j.marcinkowski@gmail.com>
commit message:
SPICE-time dependency, retrieval of spice ephemerides and rotational matrix + coordinate references.

Added functionality:
- New class renderablesphericalgrid is repurposed code from powerscaledsphere class.
  Due to z-buffer issues used as reference grid to confirm planetary orbits are correct.
  This has been a major problem as prior we had no visual reference.
  Now we have a Galactic-, Celestial- and Ecliptic-coordinate grid.
  To this also added separate shader: grid_vs.glsl / grid_fs.glsl
  These grids have a static-rotational matrix derived from partiview (thanks to Brian)
  since spice req. to-from frame to compute rotational matrix.

Time dependency:
- Added struct RuntimeData - which for now only contains openspace time and is passed to all renderables
- All renderables accept runtimeData, keep private reference and use for computation of rotational matrix
- This obviously carries corresponding changes to Scenegraph and ScenegraphNode.

Spicemanager:
- Added function that more easily provides access to rotational matrix used in spice
 (used in renderableplanet for computing planetary objects spin around axis)

Ephemeris-classes:
- Now compute ephemeris from spice based on timeepoch in runtimedata
  TODO: once z-buffer fixed - set ephemeris correctly as meters (not kilometers)

Renderengine:
- Advances time with the advanceTime method in RuntimeData struct

ISSUES:
- Our Y axis NOT same as SPICE or star-catalogue, all renderables rotated now 90deg, needs redefinition,
  lots of debugging and major headaches before this conclusion.
- Depth buffer needs to be fixed in order to properly place planets.
- Spice kernels have finite time-range, when time stops - simulation ends - ugly fix: reset time to zero.
  Possible fix: kernels de431 (part 1-2) cover huge timespan and most likely have functions to extrapolate time,
  drawback is that they are 1,7 gb each.

TODO:
- Compute and draw dynamic ephemeries for each renderable. Either do full year sweep then update for each point or
  create a tail of linesegments for each planet. Dont know yet how to do this, would like spicephemeris to be
  sub-class of Renderable (have own render() method) - good/bad?

author: Anton Arbring <antar420@student.liu.se>
commit message:
Planets shape creation & fixed texture longitude

Instead of spheres, the planets are now created as triaxial ellipsoids
according to the corresponding radii values in the SPICE kernels (if such
values are available). Apart from being more scientifically accurate, the
planets are shaped as the intersection functions in SPICE expects.

The textures will now also be aligned in longitude as in reality (w.r.t.
UTC) when using a texture map ranging from -180 in the left end to +180 on the
right, with 0 longitude in the middle (such as Greenwich in Earth texture)

commit message:
feature/time-refactor (#294)

- Change Time class to become a non-singleton
- Move ownership of the current time to TimeManager(instead of singleton access).
- Store the Time as a Syncable in TimeManager instead of representing all member variables of Time as Syncables.
- Pass a Time object around in the update/render methods, so that renderables don't have to query the OpenSpaceEngine to know if time is paused or if it jumped.
- Introduce Timeline and Keyframe classes
- Make use of Timelineand Keyframeclasses in KeyframeInteractionMode and TimeManager
- Added basic unit tests for Timelineand Keyframe

Future work: Add interpolation schemes for keyframes. Possibly use keyframes+interpolation feature to tween/morph properties, or figure out if this should be a separate mechanism.

Feature/gdalcrashfix (#331)

Saving GDAL dataset values upon initialization of dataset to avoid calling GDAL functions afterwards since it can be done concurrently. Not done for the data reading since some (not all) GDAL dataset drivers support concurrent reading. The WMS driver does not support concurrent reading, which is why we only use one worker thread per AsyncTileDataReader. Perhaps something for the future if GDAL will ensure thread saefty.

Protecting GdalRawTileDataReader with mutex lock when initializing.

Make sure read only functions in RawTileDataReader are const.

Protecting ConcurrentJobManager with mutex lock when pushing and popping to finished jobs.

commit message:
Feature/globebrowsing (#334)

Layer support for globe browsing:

Add layers using the function openspace.globebrowsing.addLayer
Delete layers using openspace.globebrowsing.deleteLayer
Layer type does not necessarily have to be of tile type. For example solidcolor does not use tiles
Blend modes for layers are Normal, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Color
Layer adjustments to affect layers. The current only active one is chroma key to cut out a color from the layer. Transfer functions or clipping masks are examples of layer adjustments for the future.
Support for adding layer specifications for quickly accessing GIBS layers:
openspace.globebrowsing.createGibsGdalXml
openspace.globebrowsing.createTemporalGibsGdalXml
The arguments for these functions are currently strings. Would it be better to use a lua dictionary?
No data values for height layers are correctly regarded (can be seen on Earth. No longer bumps on the poles)
Other minor things:

Worked a bit on point globe to render globes at large distances. Currently not in use and doesn't have anything to do with the other things.
Concurrent job manager takes a thread pool as argument and not a pointer to one. This is because the concurrent job manager needs to have ownership of the thread pool for correct deinitialization. Will cause breaking change for users of concurrent job manager if merged in to master.

commit message:
Feature/new stars rendering (#784)

 * Physically-based star rendering.
 * New Tully Pic Galaxies speck file w/o Milky Way
 * Removed PSC from stars rendering.
 * Avoiding extra calculations during shading.
 * Removed bug in billboard maximum size code.
 * New method to get the current viewport resolution. Used e.g. when rendering stereo side-by-side configuration.
 * Same as stereo stars.
 * Improved configuration.
 * Stars camera orientation.
 * Separated changes in billboards.
 * Adde min size control.
 * Setting minimum size.
 * Changed eye position. Changed data array nome inside shaders to a more accurate representation of the data.
 * Billboards reflecting actual stars sizes.
 * Scaling stars size based on luminosity, Abs Mag and size.
 * Rendering to a texture instead of fragment calculation for each star.
 * Added default parameters, new configurations and updated parameters.
 * Updated speck file handling to reflect a more general specification.
 * Added apparent magnitude from the speck files.
 * Set correct star values values for Apogee and Galah
 * Changed position from vec4 to vec3 to save GPU memory.

commit message:
Feature/offline rendering (#906)

 * Added functionality of saving out screenshots (with fixed FPS) from a recorded session during playback.
 * Test of feature to request if all data is ready to be rendered, primary used in GlobeBrowsing. Need to go over how chunkTiles are set to OK (some are never OK..).
 * Estimated having working request of checking if chunks with correct level have their color and height data loaded and ready to be rendered. Will re-enable frames saving and try making a movie.
 * Created adaptive LOD factor based on available/unavailable tile data (such that we don't run a lot of iterations with asking for a pile of data that does not fit in the tile cache).
 * Made it able to specify tile cache size in configurastion file. Renamed other Cache value to WMSCache, as we have the TileCache as well.
 * Fix for when focus node has nor renderable, when checking for if dersired data has been loaded. Should probably check all renderable/planets anyway, not just a focus object.

General CMake cleanup/overhaul

* Compile time speedup
  * Remove circular dependencies between modules and core preventing multithreaded compilation on MSVC
  * Build Spice multithreaded and as static library
  * Remove dependency from core to module-webbrowser
  * Remove unused dependency from kameleon
  * Remove additional unnecessary dependencies
  * Cleanup volume/kameleon/kameleonvolume modules
  * Fix visibility issues. Restrict include paths
  * Compile kameleon in parallel
* Other cleanup
  * Only copy CEF files from one target (hard-coded to OpenSpace right now)
  * Remove unused instrumentation code
  * Remove the ability to render AABB for globes as it caused a circular dependency between GlobeBrowsing and Debugging
  * Removing compiler and cppcheck warnings
  * Turn almost all includes into non-system includes
  * Don't warn on deprecrated copy
* Updated submodules

commit message:
Address stability problems for camera paths and make them more useful in general

* Change spline curve parameter interval from [0,1] to [0,nSegments], for slightly increased precision
* Use linear paths whenever precision isn't enough/paths are too long (and traverse linear paths differently, to make them less depending on the distance)
* Remove OrbitalNavigator.LinearFlight and instead add "Zoom to" helper functions (closes #1837 )
* Add check to prevent triggering awkward short paths, for example when flying to the current target or to the same geo position twice
* Refactor speed code and handle speed when path is shorter than start+closeup distance
* Add easing to speed dampening
* Add topic for engine mode (to be used for UI later)
* Cleaner log when creating paths (some previous info messages are now debug messages)

Related PR: OpenSpace/OpenSpace-WebGuiFrontend#70

commit message:
Add ability to cache globe data using MRFs (#2565)

Enables globe-browsing data to be cached using caching mrf's as it is loaded from the original dataset. Subsequent reads of tiles that have been cached do not query the original dataset but picks it up from the mrf data.
Supports anything that can be used a dataset for a gdal raster but raw images such as JPGs are explicitly disallowed as they lack necessary geotransform data.

Activated on a global scale by setting the following keys in openspace.cfg (ModuleConfigurations/GlobeBrowsing)
MRFCacheEnabled = true,
MRFCacheLocation = "<somepath>",
Settings can be overriden on a per-layer basis by adding the following entries to the layer entity of an asset
CacheSettings = { Enabled = true, Compression = "LERC", BlockSize = 512, Quality=25 },

The following per-layer settings are available and override the global module settings:
Enabled : enable/disable caching for this layer.
Compression: The compression algorithm to use for tile cache storage. (JPEG, PNG, or LERC)
BlockSize: Size of tiles in cache, should be a multiple of 2 although this is not required.
Quality: The quality setting of the JPEG compression (when used)

Note that heightlayers must use LERC compresison and this is the default unless overridden by a layer.

commit message:
Feature/geojson (#2595)

Add the option to add geojson components to globes, from geojson files. One geojson file creates one GeoJsonComponent, which in turn may contain multiple GlobeGeometryFeatures

Geojson is a format that supports points, lines, and polygons. In addition to the basic functionality, extra features have been added that will long-term allow rendering the geometry needed to represent KML files (another format for geospatial geometry data). Here are links to references for both formats:

    Geojson: https://geojson.org/
    KML: https://developers.google.com/kml/documentation/kmlreference

data/assets/examples/geojson includes some example files that I have used for testing. Any geojson file can also be added through drag-n-drop. Note however that you might need to change the AltitudeMode or HeightOffset properties for the feature to be visible.

commit message:
Fix: Tetramesh volume is created from structured grid

The volume is assumed to be in a structured grid looping over i,j,k (x,y,z) as such the tetrahedralizing step uses this grid to construct correctly formed tetrahedrons. The result is a volume that fits the data shape instead of a boundingbox sourrounding the data.
Adds ui sliders for rendering options

commit message:
Fix for a lot of trail related stuff (#3193)

Fixes following issues: #625 , #1067 , #1212 , #1472 , #2072 , #2235, #2964
- Trails in `renderableTrailTrajectory` now goes through the spacecraft when using `AccurateTrailPositions`.
- Trail fading controls have been improved for classes using the `renderableTrail` class.
-  `renderableOrbitalKepler` (asteroids/satellites) can now be rendered as both trails and points (or both at once). Solution implements similar functionality/controls as `renderablePointCloud`.
- Default setting for SweepChunking has been changed from `true` to `false` (iterative calculations of `renderableTrailTrajectory`).
- Some fixes related to missing points or off-by-one errors related to trail rendering

commit message:
Feature/assetvalidation (#3396)

# To run the script
Make sure to install the latest Python API version `openspace-api 0.1.2`
The script is located in `OpenSpace/support/assetvalidation`, the main script takes a few command line arguments

`--dir` - specify the OpenSpace directory 
`--filter` - optionally supply a regex string to filter which assets to validate
`--verbose` - flag to print debug info to log and also console (default off), if off only warnings and errors are logged
`--start` - flag to start OpenSpace as a subprocess (default on) if this is off it assumes OpenSpace is already running, useful if you want to run OpenSpace via Visual Studio for example. 
`--at` - specify an index to start at a specific asset

run eg: 
`python main.py --dir="C:/User/Desktop/OpenSpace" --filter="examples" --verbose=True --start=False --at=35`

commit message:
WIP: CUDA build setup with CMake

The current CUDA build setup fails due to invalid flags in the nvcc command, leading to the error:

nvcc fatal: A single input file is required for a non-link phase when an output file is specified

The problematic flags are /MP and /bigobj, which cause nvcc to misinterpret the command structure. Removing these flags allows the compilation to succeed.

Further investigation is needed to determine how they can be removed form the CMake build system.

webbrowser: Fix CEF deprecation notice and crash

According to https://github.com/chromiumembedded/cef/issues/3685, using
the so-called "Alloy bootstrap" (which seems to be the default) is
deprecated. This causes a warning when starting OpenSpace.

In some setups (e.g. an AppImage build on Ubuntu 22.04), the warning is
followed by a fatal error and a crash:

   [0505/213642.653624:FATAL:path_service.cc(265)] Failed to get the path for 1001

Following the migration instructions from the aforementioned ticket
solve both the warning and the crash.

Add time varying screen space image online class (#3646)

New screen space renderable class, ScreenSpaceTimeVaryingImageOnline, for displaying online time-dependent images from a JSON file.

This class loads a JSON file containing timestamped image URLs and displays the image that corresponds to the current simulation time. It only renders during the valid time interval defined by the dataset and updates automatically as time progresses.

Added the abilty to swap blackhole type in run time

Made it possbile to swap between kerr and Schwarzchild rendering via option property during runtime. The coordinate systems are not aligned but its hard to tell which if any of them are correcly alignd within OpenSpace, kerr should correcly align with the Y up -Z forward standard when working with OpenGL. So stars chould be alligned for kerr, but Schwarzchild is not alligned with the stars for sure and neither are probably rendering the milkyway texture in a correct orientation since it dose not account in for the position of the blackhole.

commit message:
Some rework for renderableTrailTrajectory (#3742)

Removed feature sweepChunk.
The feature was implemented for version 0.19.0 as an iterative way to calculate renderableTrailTrajectory.
However, due to the function not being active by default, and due multithreading being on the horizon for SPICE2, this code is now removed.

- Removed SweepChunk feature
- Added toggle for Accurate Trail Points (in asset: AccurateTrail)
- Changed min number of accurate points from 0 to 2
- Removed max vertices ceiling
- Fixed issue where number of vertices were not calculated properly
- Fixed point size rendering issue for RenderableTrail
- Changed start/end time for voyager 1 & 2
- Updated description for SampleInterval and TimeStampSubsampleFactor to be more clear
- Moved full sweep pass from update function to new updateBuffer function
- Fixed trail rendering issue when time is exact same as start time of a trail

commit message:
all issu and code solved  like CITATION.cff and Jenkinsfile

Issues Found & Fixed:
1. Wrong Variable Name (Line 18)

Issue: Function returned dirs instead of dirsl
Problem: The variable dirs is a loop variable, not the list being built. This would cause a runtime error.
Fix: Changed return dirs; → return dirsl;
2. Syntax Error - Extra Semicolon (Line 31)

Issue: Unnecessary semicolon after closing brace: };
Problem: Inconsistent syntax style and could cause parsing issues
Fix: Removed the semicolon after the if block
3. Missing Semicolon (Line 129)

Issue: deleteDir() missing semicolon
Problem: Inconsistent code formatting, potential syntax issues
Fix: Added semicolon: deleteDir();
4. Wrong CMake Flag (Line 136)

Issue: Used -DMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release instead of -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
Problem: Typo in CMake variable name would cause build configuration to fail silently
Fix: Changed -DMAKE_BUILD_TYPE → -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE
5. Trailing Backslash (Line 154)

Issue: Extra backslash at end of line: 'bin/Debug/codegentest');\
Problem: Syntax error that would break the pipeline
Fix: Removed the trailing backslash
6-9. Wrong Path Separators on macOS (Lines 159, 164, 333, 338)

Issue: Used Windows backslashes (\) in macOS test paths
Problem: Paths would not resolve correctly on macOS systems
Fix: Changed all macOS paths to use forward slashes:
'bin/Debug\\SGCTTest' → 'bin/Debug/SGCTTest'
'bin/Debug\\GhoulTest' → 'bin/Debug/GhoulTest'
All fixes improve code correctness, consistency, and ensure the Jenkins pipeline builds and tests properly across Windows, macOS, and Linux platforms.

Issues Found & Fixed:
1. Invalid Field in preferred-citation (Line 33)

Issue: Used non-standard field scope with duplicate type declaration
Problem: CFF format doesn't recognize scope as a valid field for preferred-citation; it's redundant with the top-level message

commit message:
Separation of Assets (#3993)

This PR changes the organization of a whole bunch of asset files that were difficult to do in individual PRs and would have increase the testing time.

  - Asset separation: Many assets before defined the object, the trail, sometimes a label and sometimes actions in the same asset, meaning that it was impossible to get, for example, the trail for an object without also loading the labels. The following asset groups have been split up. The previous asset is now a "meta" asset that includes the other new asset files. In many cases this also caused the introduction of a subfolder to hold the new assets (except for regular planets)   For example:  ->  `mars.asset` -> `globe.asset` + `trail.asset` + `label.asset` + `actions.asset` + `mars.asset` and the new `mars.asset` includes all other four.
    - Dwarf planets (special: If a dwarf planet is specified as a RenderableGlobe, the new asset is `globe.asset`; if it is a model, it is `model.asset`
    - Planets
    - Major and Minor moons of planets
    - The Sun
    - ISS, Hubble, Tiangong, Aqua, SNPP, and Terra
    - Interstellar objects
  - Some naming harmonization specifically with the dwarf planets to export the objects as their correct name
  - All minor moons for gas planets are now in the `minor` subfolder and each group has received its own subfolder
  - Harmonizing naming of variables in asset files (using `xAsset` when requiring an asset from another folder, using the file name if requiring something from the same folder)
  - No longer use `../..` or longer relative paths as they were hard to maintain. Use explicit paths. Single `..` are still in place 
  - Don't explicitly `Enabled = false` labels, but use `Enabled = asset.enabled` and use the `false` on the meta asset
  - Only use `asset.enabled` in the second-to-last meta asset.  It was causing a lot of warnings otherwise when meta assets (particularly for layers) were included from multiple places
  - Moving the Server-location detection into all `default_layers.asset`s
  - Merge Saturn 2025 discoveries two asset files into a single

# Breaking Changes
## Scene Graph Nodes
  - Exporting all objects using their Identifier rather than a custom name
  - `ErisGlobe` -> `ErisModel`

in the created files. As before, it casts the type

(with argument sanitize=True), so that the input dict
is first sanitized (modified in-place) and then checked
against the specs.

These changes increase consistency and robustness of
save_photon_hdf5() regardless of the variability in
the input data.

author: ramenbytes <36470445+ramenbytes@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Ensure h5file is closed if requested

Callers of the save_photon_hdf5() can specify that they wanted the hdf5
file they passed in closed before returning. However, we performed
validation before closing the file, and the validation can error out. If
this happened, the file /would not be closed/. Not a bit deal if the
user still had a hold on the file object and could close it themselves,
but if they instead passed in just the file name then they were unable
to close it themselves without somehow getting a hold of the object from
python's global list of open files. This meant that they would need to
restart the python process before they could try saving to the hdf5 file
again.

Now, we place the file closing logic in the clause of a finally:
statement to ensure we always close it if the user wants us to.

commit message:
Improved handling of fine classes and single characters.

Previously, inputs such as (UK) postcodes were not handled that well.
Giving Rexpy

        ['EH3 1LH', 'G4 2BP',]

as inputs would result in the RE:

        r'^[A-Z0-9]{2,3}\ [A-Z0-9]{3}$']

This is correct, but rather loose, as Rexpy has failed to notice that
the pattern is really

       LETTER(s) DIGIT SPACE DIGIT LETTERS(2)

and merely said

        LETTERS-OR_DIGITS SPACE LETTERS-OR-DIGITS(3)

The algorithm has been refined a bit, and it can now spot patterns like these.
It remains far from perfect, but will now often produce tigher REs. In the
case above, for example, it now produces:

        r'^[A-Z]{1,2}\d\ \d[A-Z]{2}$']

which is exactly what a human would probably come up with.

Some test results have been updated accordingly, and some new tests have
been added. Another nice improve is for names (ordinarily capitalized),
where now examples like

        ['Albert Einstein', 'Richard Feynman', 'Miles Davis']

will now produce

        r'^[A-Z][a-z]{4,6}\ [A-Z][a-z]+$'

rather than

        r'^[A-Za-z]{5,7}\ [A-Za-z]+$'

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Various fixes to the Pandas implementation of constraint discovery/verify.

  - It now deals with boolean field types 'sloppily' by default (the same
    as it does with integers), since Pandas uses a real field to hold booleans
    if there are nulls present.

  - When reading a CSV file to build a dataframe, it now does a better job
    with date-valued fields. The underlying Pandas CSV reader reads them in
    as strings (even when told to infer dates, and even when given an explicit
    date parsing hint), because its behaviour is to only read columns as dates
    if it has been explicitly told the names of date columns in advance.
    But TDDA can do a better job of that, by looking at string-valued fields
    after they've been read, and converting them to dates if they can be.

  - Added some 'help' to the type recognition by making it even more sloppy,
    for string fields that contain completely numeric values. Pandas will
    have read them in as integer (or real) fields, but, armed with additional
    information (in the form of constraints), TDDA can infer that it made a
    poor choice of type when reading from the CSV file, and 'stringify' the
    result when doing a verification. This doesn't loosen the constraint,
    really, since the choice of how to interpret the contents of the CSV file
    isn't part of the CSV file itself - it's an interpretation put on by the
    TDDA code when its reading a CSV file.

  - Added some more unit-tests.

commit message:
Add new setting variableLengthGroups to rexpy's extract/Extractor.

This is False by default, retaining previous behaviour.

When set to True, rexpy will allow regular-expression fragments
to include optional bits on the end (which has not been the case
hitherto), e.g. 'https?'.

This is sometimes helpful, but not always. (In particular, it can
make Rexpy produce less general regular expressions when small
numbers of examples are provided). When it's a bit better, we will
probably add a command-line flag to control this, and perhaps make
it the default.

There are also minor enhancements in generating regular expressions,
so that ? is used instead of {0,1} (it wasn't previously actually
ever generated, but can be now), and also so that single repeats
of letters in single-character non-fixed fragments will be expanded
rather than using {2}, e.g. 'https?' will be used rather than 'ht{2}ps?'.

commit message:
New flags for rexpy + minor refactoring.

New flags are:

  -V (or --verbose)  for more verbosity while generating regular expressions
  -VV(or --Verbose)  even more verbosity while generating regular expressions

  -vlf (or --variable)  for variable-length fragments.
                        There isn't a great name for this yet: it's an
                        approach to getting more detailed regular expressions.

  -flf (or --fixed)     fixed-length fragments.
                        This is the current default and the reverse of -vlf.

author: Nicholas J. Radcliffe <njr@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Improved support for accented characters in rexpy.

This involved various changes:

    - All regular expressions are now (and should be, in Python)
      compiled/used with the re.U or re.UNICODE flag

    - When accented characters are found, a fancy version of \w is
      used to match them. In particular, a possibly accented letter,
      of either case, from any alphabet, is matched with [^\W0-9_].
      (This is a bit ugly, but works.)

    - Rexpy now has a notion of a (possibly-) accented letter,
      and a possibly-accented alphanumeric character.
      The possibly-accented letter may include digits from other
      alphabets as we haven't yet found a way (using the standard re
      library) to exclude them.

    - If the regex library is installed, this is used in preference
      to re. This currently has no effect, but it does have support
      for more specific international characters, including Alphabetic
      characters, so we may take advantage of that (at least optionally)
      in the future.

    - The handling of capture groups has become a little more complex,
      as we now sometimes generate nested capture groups, making
      counting them more complex.

    - A few extra tests have been added, specifically for accented
      characters and the capture group handling.

    - A minor bug in the character class hierarchy has been fixed.

    - The version number has been bumped to 0.5.0

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Added support for running subsets of TDDA reference tests, rather than
always running them all.

This is useful during development (of analysis and tests), and is also
useful for limited regeneration of results (when a change requires the
results to be regenerated, but only for a specific test or tests).

When run with the --tagged option on the command line, only tests (or
test classes) that have been decorated with @tag are run. The -1 option
is a shorthand for --tagged.

When run with the --istagged option on the command line, no tests are
run, but the names of all the classes that have been tagged are listed.

To tag a unittest test or class, use the @tag decorator, as in the
following example:

    from tdda.referencetest.referencetestcase import ReferenceTestCase, tag

    # tag an entire test class;
    # all tests in this class will run when --tagged is used.
    @tag
    class MyTests1(ReferenceTestCase):
        ...

    class MyTests2(ReferenceTestCase):
        # tag an individual test in a test class;
        # only test_a will run when --tagged is used.
        @tag
        def test_a(self):
            ...

        def test_b(self):
            ...

Tagged tests (for running subsets) is only available under unittest
at present, not under pytest yet.

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Added support for TDDA constraint verification to be run as a 'detector'.

This extends the verification process by producing an output dataset,
containing information about which input records have failed any constraints.

On the command line, 'tdda verify' now takes some additional optional
flags to specify that detected failures should be written to a separate
flat file (or feather file), along with various other optional flags to
control the details of what should get written to that file, namely:

    - Whether or not to include a record number column to identify records
    - Whether or not to include detailed per-constraint 'ok' fields, in
      addition to an 'n_failures' field giving the total number of failed
      constraints per record.
    - What fields from the input file to include in the output file
    - Whether to write out a line for every record, or just failing ones

Using the API, the verify_df() function takes various additional optional
parameters to specify 'detection'. From the API, you don't have to write
the detected records to a file; you can get access to them as a separate
Pandas DataFrame, or you can specify that the detection columns should be
added 'in_place' to the input DataFrame.

This is currently only implemented for the Pandas Dataframe case (including
flat files and feather files from the command-line tools), not database
tables.

commit message:
When running verify detection, empty and remove the output file first.

This means that you get early notification if you specify an output file
that you can't write to. (It'll fail right at the start, rather than at
the end, after a lot of time-consuming processing).

It also means you don't get left with an out-of-date output file containing
detections from a previous run, if you run it and nothing is detected (and
therefore no output file is written).

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Fixed bugs with epsilon in constraint verify, and with detection ok fields.

The epsilon flag was being ignored (both through the API and the command
line), because comparisons were always being done in 'closed' mode, and
there was no way to override that. Now, all comparisons are done in 'fuzzy'
mode (which means that they're 'closed' if epsilon is zero, and tolerant
otherwise). The default value for epsilon is now zero, so that, along with
the change above, means that the flag now works as expected.

The detection 'ok' fields were being created with the wrong type (should be
boolean, not real), and that's fixed now.

The 'nonnull' and 'nodups' ones were more fundamentally broken in that they
were being computed in a way that meant that sometimes they could be null
(NaN). That was wrong, and is now fixed too.

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
constraint detection now generates appropriate Index/RowNumber in output.

When a row number is required (with --rownumber, or without --output-fields):

  * If input is CSV and output is CSV, the row-number field is called
    RowNumber, and is the row number from input, starting from 1 (since the
    header line was row zero).

  * If input is CSV and output is Feather, there's no explcit row-number field
    in the output file, but the generated dataframe has an index called Index,
    with values taken from the index of the input (which will start from zero).

  * If input is Feather and output is CSV, the row-number field is called
    Index, and is taken from the index of the input dataframe.

  * If input is Feather and output is Feather, there's no explicit row-number
    field in the output dataframe, but the generated dataframe has an index
    called Index, with values taken from the index of the input (which may
    not necessarily start at 0, and could even be a hierarchical multi-value
    index).

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Added better control of rownumber in detection output, and boolean fields.

The rownumber produced by detection now takes account of both where the
data originated and where the detection output is being written to:

There are four cases

  1. CSV -> CSV.  The output field RowNumber is the row-number from the input.
  3. Feather -> CSV. The output field Index comes from the index on the input.
  2. CSV -> Feather. The output index comes from the thw-number from the input.
  4. Feather -> Feather. The output index comes from the index on the input.

Also added an optional --int flag (or boolean_ints=True via the API) for
detection, to write out boolean values as integers to CSV files, rather than
as "true" and "false" values. This is useful for cases where the CSV file
is going to be consumed by some other process that can't read booleans.

commit message:
Fixed bug in tdda.referencetest.ReferenceTest.set_default_data_location.

It was supposed to apply at a per-class level (so if you call it on the
base ReferenceTest class, then it affects ALL tests in all subclasses, but
if you call it just on your subclass, then it only affects that subclass,
plus any sub-subclasses of that which don't themselves override it).

But that's now how it was implemented. It was always applying the defaults
to the base class, and using those in all subclasses. So that meant that
if you used on it a large project, with a number of different test-data
locations for different submodules, then you couldn't do that (except by
explcitly setting the data location within each individual instance, bacause
the class-based defaults weren't working right).

They're now working right. Also added an extra test to test this.

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
Modified the Pandas-based constraint commands to allow '-' as file.

A '-' means stdin on input, and stdout on output.

Signature for tdda discover is now:
    tdda discover input [output]
where both input and output can be '-'.

Signature for tdda verify is now:
    tdda verify input [constraints [output]]
where both input and output can be '-', and constraints is inferred from
input if it can be.

Signature for tdda detect is now
    tdda detect input [constraints [output]]
where both input and output can be '-'
where both input and output can be '-', and constraints is inferred from
input if it can be.

So these commands can now be used as follows:

    tdda discover - [-]            (discover from stdin, write json to stdout)
    tdda verify - constraints [-]  (read from stdin, verify against constraints)
    tdda detect - constraints [-]  (read from stdin, verify against constraints
                                    and write failures to stdout)

Also fixed issue with boolean fields that contain nulls. They were being
misinterpreted as being string fields, but then failing (because they
weren't really string fields). Booleans with missing values are now just
booleans. Tests for this now updated.

author: Simon Brown <simon@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
The ignore_patterns parameter is now treated slightly more strictly than
before, and has had its documentation improved. If you provide an unanchored
regular expression pattern, it now requires that both sides match that
pattern, but it ALSO now requires that the remaining parts, to the left and
right of where the pattern matched, be 'equivalent' if the line is to be
ignored. The two 'left parts' must be equivalent, and the two 'right parts'
must also be equivalent. This 'equivalence' is checked by (recursively)
applying the same logic to these sub-parts.

The ignore_substrings parameter is now treated slightly more strictly than
before. Previously, a line was ignored if it contained any of the ignorable

commit message:
Changed 'test' command to from 'this' Python rather than a new Python.

Previously, the 'test' command (run with 'tdda test') ran in a subshell
using an os.system call. In order to do this, we used sys.executable()
to find (ostensibly) the path to the running version of Python.

It transpires, however, that sys.executable() does not always return
the path to the running Python...and indeed sometimes returns a path
that does not exist. We now, therefore, simply run the tests in the
current Python, by calling the (new) function 'testall', now used
by main() in tdda.testtdda.py.

Dialect support expanded.

Supported dialect are:

  perl:               As above

commit message:
Updated bracket generatation ("character classes: [...]").

We now use almost no escaping for characters in character classes,
instead using special rules to force
  - close square bracket ("]") to the start
  - dash (hyphen "-") to the end
  - carat ("^") away from the start
Only backslash is now normally escaped in character classes.

There is also embryonic provision for new dialects "javascript" and "ruby"
to force escaping of "]" in character classes, since they don't appear to
obey the normal rules, but the embryonic provision isn't really used by
anything (or available outside the API) at this point.

Many tests have been updated as a result. Many tests also now check,
to a greater extent than was previously the case, that the regular expressions
generated actually actually match the strings used to generate them and
(equally relevantly) don't match certain strings you might worry they would
match if you weren't fully "au fait" with the details of regex rules!

 - assertCasesEqual:    Check multiple named case,

 - checkFunctionByArg:  Check a single-arg function with

 - checkFunctionByKWArgs: As previous, but using named

author: Nick Radcliffe <njr@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
2.2 release. Change notes:

* **2.2** Improvements to parquet file handling.

* **2.2** Have not (as threatened) removed for feather files yet
  but will shortly, possibly even before 2.3, but a deprecation
  warning has been added that shows when feather files are used.

* **2.2** Added parquet files to various of the examples that users
  get with `tdda examples`

* **2.2** Fixed problem with categorical strings from parquet.

* **2.2** Now use chardet to figure out (infer/guess)  encodings in `gentest`

* **2.2** Added partial support for CSVW metadata (for CSV files)
  and some tests and test data in CSVW format.

* **2.2** Extended support for writing temporary files when tests fails
  from strings/text files to dataframes, CSV files and Parquet files.
  This also means that the dataframe methods can now re-write reference
  results using -W/--write-all etc.

* **2.2** Renamed some methods and parameters for DataFrame assertions
  and comparisons. In particular
   - `assertOnDiskDataFrameCorrect` replaces assertCSVFileCorrect,
     with the path name not being `ref_path` rather than `ref_csv`.
     The old method remains, and calls the new method.
     The new methods works with parquet files as well as with CSV files.
   - `assertOnDiskDataFramesCorrect` replaces assertCSVFilesCorrect,
     with the path name not being `ref_paths` rather than `ref_csvs`.
     The old method remains, and calls the new method.
     The new methods works with parquet files as well as with CSV files.

* **2.2** Better reporting of differences between data frames when
  tests fail or comparisons show differences.

* **2.2** Added experimental `tdda diff` command for comparing data frames
  serialized as parquiet or CSV files.

* **2.2** Add rich dependency and use rich to format dataframe diffs.

* **2.2** Fixed bug in flag parsing that prevented multiple
  single-character flags to be used separately, rather than combined.
  (So `-1W` worked byt -1 -W` did not.)

* **2.2** Fixed bug in the metadata written in constraints files.
  The local and utc times were supposed to be written in ISO8601
  format, but repeated %H in the format string instead of using %M.
  Switched to use `.isoformat()`, and accepted its default `T`
  separator in the datestamps, rather than sticking with space.

* **2.2** Quite a lot of internal refactoring, making parameters
  and methods names more consistent, and better suited to a wider
  variety of file formats and back-end implementations.

author: Nick Radcliffe <njr@StochasticSolutions.com>
commit message:
fuzzy_nulls!

Extended pandas metadata tests further (still with extremely
simple cases) and added fuzzy_nulls as an option to
pandas dataframe comparisons (not yet to cli).

fuzzy_nulls defaults to False, but if set to object
will map nulls in object cols with strings to ''
and also the column they are being compared to,
even if this is string. If we to True, it does
the same for string columns.

This basically says "Pandas doesn't really understand
the difference between empty strings and nulls in CSV
files, so we;ll treat them as equivalent.
